THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT,
AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:08-03-2011 PASSED IN WC/F No.45/2007 ON THE FILE OF THE LABOUR OFFICER AND COMMISSIONER FOR WORKMENS COMPENSATION, GADAG DISTRICT, GADAG, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.2,67,908/- WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 12% P.A. FROM 30-06-2006 TILL ITS DEPOSIT.
 THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 20.01.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the petitioner in WC/F No.45/2007 aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 08.03.2011 passed by the Labour Officer and Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation,
Gadag (for short referred to as "the Commissioner").
2.
The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Commissioner for the sake of convenience.

3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
It was contended that the deceased husband of the petitioner i.e., Jafarsab Gudawal was under the employment of respondents 1 and 2.

That on 31.05.2006, on instructions given by respondents 1 and 2, the husband of the petitioner was assisting a mason for repairing Zinc sheets in the textile Mill owned by them and while he was getting down from top floor to carry sand and cement, he fell from the floor on account of breaking of a plastic sheet and on the way to hospital, he succumbed to the injuries sustained by him.

It was contended that the deceased was earning Rs.4,500/-
per month and the petitioner was solely depending on him.

It was contended that the respondents 1 and 2 before the Commissioner are the owner and proprietor of the said Textile Mill and respondent No.3 is the insurer and since the deceased husband of the petitioner died during the course and arising out of employment, the respondents are liable to pay compensation and thus, the petitioner filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
The Manager vs Smt. Razia Begaum W/O Jafarsab Gadwal on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2576426/
2 4.

On issuance of notice by the Commissioner, the respondents 1 to 3 appeared before the Commissioner through their respective counsels and filed their objections denying the averments of the petition as false and untenable and called upon the petitioner to prove the allegations.
The respondents 1 and 2 admitted that they were employers of deceased-Jafarsab and he was a weaver in their textile mill.
They also stated that he was assisting a mason for repairing a zinc sheet and while he was on duty in the mill, the mishap occurred resulting in his death.

However, respondents 1 and 2 contended that the textile mill was covered under insurance issued by respondent No.3 and therefore, any liability has to be fastened upon the respondent No.3.
5.
The respondent No.3 insurance company contended that the deceased-Jafarsab was not in employment and that the petitioner be put to strict proof of the contentions taken up in the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Commissioner framed necessary issues and evidence was led before the Commissioner.
The petitioner was examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to P17 were marked in evidence.

In order to disprove the case of the petitioner the son of respondent No.2 as PA holder of respondent No. 2 was examined as RW1(described as RW2 in the deposition sheet) and respondent No.2 was examined as RW2 (not offered for cross examination) and got marked five documents as Ex.R2(1) to (5) on his behalf.
The insurance company examined one of its officials as RW3 and got marked a copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3(1).

After hearing the arguments by both sides, the Commissioner awarded the compensation of Rs.2,67,908/- to the petitioner along with interest @ 12% per annum after one month from the date of the incident till the date of deposit.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, the insurer has approached this Court in this appeal.

7. The appellant contended that the learned Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation has committed an error in coming to the conclusion that the incident happened is arising out of and in the course of employment.

It was further contended that the learned Commissioner has committed an error in fixing the liability on the insurance company by taking Rs.3,500/- per month as wages paid to the deceased-Jafarsab in the absence of any documentary evidence on record.

It is contended that the claim is under workmen compensation policy and the employer has declared seven employees salary as Rs.50,000/- per year and paid premium on that amount and therefore, by calculating the monthly salary of each employees it comes to Rs.596/- per month.
Therefore, the liability of the insurance company to pay the compensation would be by calculating the compensation taking monthly salary at Rs.596/- only.
Therefore, it has contended that the insurance company is liable to pay a sum of Rs.45,594/- only and rest of the compensation has to be paid by the employer.

It is further contended that the insurance company is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation as the liability is covered under the contractual obligations under the policy and there was no liability to interest on the compensation.
8. On issuance of notice, respondents 1 and 2 appeared before this Court through their counsel.
But respondent No.3 did not appear despite service of notice.
9. The appeal has been admitted on 19.06.2015 and the Trial Court records were secured.
The arguments by learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company and the respondents 1 and 2 herein were heard.

The Manager vs Smt. Razia Begaum W/O Jafarsab Gadwal on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2576426/
3 10.

The learned counsel for the appellant herein, in his submissions before this Court, urged two grounds viz., it was a textile industry and therefore, weaving was the work of the employee but the deceased-Jafarsab was assisting a mason for the repairs of roofing, which was not in the course of employment and thus, the insurance policy do not cover the risks involved in such activities which is unconnected to the employment of the deceased.

The second point urged by the insurance company is that the policy was covering 7 persons who had annual wages of Rs.50,000/- and therefore, the monthly income of each of the employee would come only to Rs.596/- per month and the policy being a contractual policy, appellant-insurance company is liable to pay a sum of Rs.45,594/- only.
On the said analogy that it was a contractual obligation, the insurance company is also not liable to pay the interest to the petitioners.

11. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 contended that the incident took place in the premises of the textile mill owned by them and the deceased was an employee in the said textile mill.
At the instructions of the employer, he was assisting a mason, who was repairing the roof of the mill.
Therefore, assisting a mason in a textile mill definitely covers the definition of 'workman' and as such, the contention raised by the insurance company is not tenable.
It is further contended that the second point raised by the appellant-insurance company that each of the seven employees covered under the policy cannot be equated in their salary and the job.
It is submitted that out of seven employees, some of the employees may be entitled for higher wages and some of them for lesser wages.

It is submitted that depending on the skill sets, their wages and pay may vary and therefore, when the policy do not define the skilled or un-skilled, the insurance company cannot raise a contention that each of the employee was being paid a salary of Rs.596/- per month.

It is contended that those seven employees may be a mestry, helper, assistant, weaver etc.,
and therefore, the insurance company cannot raise such a contention.

Further, it is submitted that there existed master and servant relationship and therefore, the employers are liable to pay interest and consequently, the insurance company is also liable to pay the interest to indemnify the employer.
It is contended that the relationship of the master and servant between the deceased and the employer is well established by virtue of PF returns and advice produced by the petitioner.
Therefore, it is contended that the appeal is bereft of any merits and same is liable to be dismissed.
12. It is pertinent to note that the evidence of the employer has been recorded by the commissioner as RW2.

His evidence discloses that the deceased was an employee as a weaver in the textile mill owned by respondents 1 and 2 but he was directed by respondents 1 and 2 to assist a mason, who was repairing the roof of the mill and while he was supplying sand and cement for the roofing, the mishap occurred and on the way to the hospital, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
It is consistent case of the - 10 - employer that the deceased was an employee.
In support of his contention, he has produced the PF returns and the advice in respect of Employees' Provident Fund Scheme issued by the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner.
These documents clearly establish that the deceased was an employee in the mill owned by the respondents 1 and 2.
It is also relevant to note that the official of the insurance company i.e., the appellant herein was examined as RW3 before the Commissioner.

The Manager vs Smt. Razia Begaum W/O Jafarsab Gadwal on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2576426/
4
He has not denied that the deceased was not under the employment of respondents 1 and 2.
The contention was that, the deceased-Jafarsab was not the workman/employee within the meaning of law.
In support of such contention and except the oral testimony of RW3, nothing is placed on record.

Under these circumstances, the evidence of the employer who is examined as RW2 gains importance and it is not in the domain of the appellant-insurance company to contradict the fact that the deceased was not an employee.
Further, a permanent employee of the mill assisting a mason, who was repairing roof, definitely comes within the purview of the - 11 - scope of the employment.
A straight jacket formula that a weaver has to do the work of weaving only and nothing else would be absurd preposition.
Up keeping of the premises of the employment definitely come within the scope of the employment.
Therefore, this contention raised by the appellant herein is not sustainable under law.
13. The second contention raised by the appellant is regarding the terms and conditions of the policy.
The said policy is produced at Ex.R3.
It is pertinent to note that Ex.R3 shows that the premium details for employees with wages more than Rs.4,000/- is shown to be seven.
Conspicuously, it is not mentioned as to whether the wages are Rs.4,000/- per month or per annum.
It is also relevant to note that any policy or contract cannot be oblivious to the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, at no stretch of imagination it can be said that the wages mentioned in Ex.R3 was Rs.4,000/- per annum.
If it is divided by 12 months, the monthly wages comes to Rs.596/- as contended by the appellant-insurance company.

Monthly wages of Rs.596/-
cannot be accepted in view of the fact that the Minimum - 12 - Wages Act prescribed wages of at least Rs.150/- per day.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant-insurance company that Ex.R3 prescribed the wages of each of the seven workmen covered under the policy to be Rs.596/- per month cannot be accepted.
Moreover, the Ex.R3(1) do not mention any terms and conditions of the policy.
Under these circumstances, this Court is unable to accept the contention of the appellant herein.

14. The learned Commissioner has considered the income of the deceased-Jafarsab at Rs.3,500/-
per month in the absence of any acceptable documentary evidence.
He has also observed that it is in accordance with Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, I do not find any reason to interfere in the finding given by the learned Commissioner that the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.3,500/- per month.
Therefore, the calculation of the compensation amount by the Commissioner at a sum of Rs.2,67,908/- deserves to be confirmed.
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the interest on the compensation amount could not have been fastened upon the insurance company.

In this regard, he has placed reliance on The Manager vs Smt. Razia Begaum W/O Jafarsab Gadwal on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2576426/
5

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Smt. Nagarathna and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, the Single Bench of this Court by placing reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of P.J.Narayan v. Union of India2, held that the insurer is not statutorily required to cover the liability of interest in respect of the subject matter of the insurance.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as follows:
"This writ petition is for the purposes of directing the insurance company to delete the clause in the insurance policy which provides that in cases of compensation under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, the insurance company will not be liable to pay interest.
We see no substance in the writ petition.
There is no statutory liability on the insurance company.
The statutory liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act is on the employer.
An insurance is a matter of contract between the ILR 2003 KAR 4825 (2006) 5 SCC 200 - 14 - insurance company and the insured.
It is always open to the insurance company to refuse to insure.
Similarly, they are entitled to provide by contract that they will not take on liability for interest.
In the absence of any statute to that effect, insurance companies cannot be forced by courts to take on liabilities which they do not want to take on.
The writ petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs."
16. In that view of the matter, the insurance company cannot be saddled with the interest.
It is worth to note that the employer i.e. respondents 2 and 3 herein are not statutorily required to have a insurance under the Employees' Compensation Act.

Therefore, the question whether the employer has to be indemnified in respect of interest also being a subject matter of the contractual obligations,
is to be left open to be agitated between them.
17. In the case on hand, the sum of Rs.2,67,908/- as determined by the learned Commissioner has been deposited by the insurance company before this Court.

Now the said amount has to be paid to the petitioner-Smt. Razia Begum W/o. Jafarsab Gadawal i.e. respondent No.1 herein with a liberty to her to recover the interest as ordered by the - 15 - Commissioner from the employers i.e. respondents 2 and 3 herein.

18. In view of the above, the appeal deserves be allowed in part by absolving the appellant-insurance company from paying interest to the petitioner and clarifying the same that the interest has to be borne by the employers.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.

The determination of compensation for a sum of Rs.2,67,908/- made by the learned Labour Officer and the commissioner for workmen's compensation, Gadag is hereby The Manager vs Smt. Razia Begaum W/O Jafarsab Gadwal on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2576426/
6 confirmed.
However, the interest on the said compensation amount beyond the period of 30 days from the date of the incident @ 12% is liable to be paid by the employers i.e. respondents 2 and 3 herein.

The amount in deposit before this Court is ordered to be disbursed to the petitioner-Smt.Razia Begum W/o. Jafarsab Gadawal i.e. respondent No.1 herein on due identification, preferably through electronic money transfer.
The petitioner to furnish the bank account details to the Registry.
- 16 - In view of disposal of the appeal, pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and are disposed off accordingly.
